---
title: "Concept classification"
---

```{r setup}
source("_common.R")
clusters <- targets::tar_read(clusters, store = store)
labels <- targets::tar_read(llm_labels, store = store)
audit_summary <- targets::tar_read(audit_summary, store = store)
audit_sample <- targets::tar_read(audit_sample, store = store)
```

Seed patterns only find concepts that someone already thought of. To find
the rest, distinct attribute definitions within each DimensionVector family
are clustered. Each definition is represented by **TF-IDF** weights over the
family's most common terms, and the definitions are grouped with **seeded
k-means**. Large families are sampled with a fixed seed. Protocol:
`r doc_link("llm-protocol.md", "LLM and audit protocol")`.

## Clusters

`exemplars` lists the definitions closest to each cluster centre, separated
by `||`.

```{r clusters}
cluster_table <- clusters$clusters |>
  dplyr::left_join(labels, by = "cluster_id")
shared <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(cluster_table)
filtered_table(
  crosstalk::filter_select("dv", "Dimension vector", shared, ~dimension_vector),
  reactable::reactable(
    shared,
    searchable = TRUE, compact = TRUE, striped = TRUE, resizable = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = 10,
    columns = list(exemplars = wide(520), top_terms = wide(240), units = wide(240))
  )
)
```

## LLM labels

```{r llm-status}
llm_status <- dplyr::count(labels, llm_status, name = "clusters")
knitr::kable(llm_status)
```

LLM labeling is **off by default**. It sends cluster exemplars (public EML
text) to a third-party API and costs money. When enabled in `config.yml`,
each cluster gets a structured label: measured concept, entity or medium,
process, denominator semantics, coherence, whether it is a QK candidate,
aligned vocabulary terms, confidence, and rationale. Labels are cached as
`targets` and recorded with the model and prompt hash.

## Human audit

`audit_sample.csv` holds a seeded, stratified sample of
`r nrow(audit_sample)` attributes (a fixed number per cluster). Reviewers
copy rows into `data/reference/audit_reviewed.csv` and fill in
`reviewer_measured_concept`, `reviewer_agrees` (yes or no), and
`reviewer_notes`. The pipeline then reports agreement by family below.
Families with low agreement are re-scoped or kept manual.

```{r audit}
if (nrow(audit_summary) == 0) {
  htmltools::p(htmltools::em("No audit rows reviewed yet."))
} else {
  interactive_table(audit_summary, "audit_summary")
}
```
